summary: This document defines the Content-ID header field for SIP. It also updates RFC 5621, which only allowed a Content-ID URL to point at a body part within a multipart body, so the URL can also refer to a complete message body and its metadata.

plainLanguage.summary: It lets one part of a SIP message give a name tag to another part, or to the whole message, so they can point to each other.

questions: what is the sip content-id header
how to reference a sip message body
can a sip proxy change content-id
subtitle: A SIP header field that names a whole message body, so other headers can point to it.

tldr.problem: A Content-ID URL could only point to one body part inside a multipart SIP body, so a sender with a single piece of content still had to wrap it in a multipart body just to give it a reference.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8262 defines Content-ID as a SIP header field that identifies the complete message-body and its metadata, and updates RFC 5621, RFC 5368 and RFC 6442 to allow referencing a whole message-body.
tldr.outcome: A SIP message can carry one non-multipart body and still be referenced by a Content-ID URL. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and is not obsoleted.

facts.label: Proxies
facts.value: MUST NOT add, modify or delete it

today: RFC 8262 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2017. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of the SIP Content-ID header field.

sections.title: Body Parts and Content-ID URLs
sections.content:
A SIP message has a start-line, header fields, an empty line and an optional message-body (RFC 3261). The body can be multipart or not. A multipart body contains body parts in the MIME format, and each part may carry a Content-ID header field with a unique ID.

A SIP header field can point at a body part with a Content-ID URL (RFC 2392). For example, RFC 6442 has a Geolocation header field point at a part holding location information, and RFC 5368 has a Refer-To header field point at a part holding a list of targets.
sections.plainLanguage: A body part is like a sticker-labelled envelope inside a bigger package, and a Content-ID URL says which labelled envelope you mean.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content:
How to identify a complete message-body with a Content-ID header field, and how to reference it with a Content-ID URL, was never specified. In RFC 5621 the URL references a specific body part only.

The consequence is wasteful. A UAC that sends an INVITE with location by value and no SDP offer has only one MIME entity to send, but because the Geolocation header must reference a body part, it wraps that entity in a multipart body with a single part. The same happens with a REFER that carries a list of targets.

Some existing specifications, such as RFC 5368, contain examples that show a SIP Content-ID header field referencing a complete message-body even though that was never specified. Many implementors read the examples as allowing it. This document makes the normative language say so explicitly.
sections.plainLanguage: It is like having to put one letter inside a box just so it can have a label. This RFC lets you label the letter itself.

sections.title: The Content-ID Header Field
sections.content:
The syntax is Content-ID = "Content-ID" HCOLON msg-id, where msg-id = "<" id-left "@" id-right ">". The syntax is simplified compared to RFC 5322 to disallow comments. The value must be unique within a given SIP message, including any embedded MIME Content-ID values. It need not be unique across messages and has no meaning outside the message that carries it.

Used as a SIP header field, Content-ID identifies the message-body together with the metadata provided by a MIME-Version header field (if present) and by any header fields with a Content- prefix, including Content-ID itself. The body it identifies can be multipart or non-multipart. It can appear in any SIP message that is allowed to contain a message-body.
sections.plainLanguage: The tag has to be different from every other tag in the same message, but it only matters inside that one message.

sections.title: User Agent and Proxy Procedures
sections.content:
A UA MAY include a Content-ID header field in any SIP message that is allowed to contain a message-body, and MUST NOT include one in a message that is not. The UA MUST set the value to something unique within that message.

A proxy MUST NOT add, modify or delete a Content-ID header field.

For backward compatibility, if an existing specification only defines carrying a single body part in a multipart body for a Content-ID URL to reference, implementations MUST NOT put the MIME entity in a non-multipart body unless that specification is updated to explicitly allow it.
sections.plainLanguage: The sender writes the name tag. The people who pass the message along must leave it exactly as it is.

sections.title: Updates to Other RFCs
sections.content:
Three RFCs are updated with OLD and NEW text.

  • RFC 5621, Section 9.1: a Content-ID URL may now point to a body part or to the message-body and the header fields describing it.
  • RFC 5368, Section 7: the Refer-To pointer may target the body part or the message-body carrying the URI list, and either a MIME Content-ID header field (RFC 4483) or a SIP Content-ID header field can label it.
  • RFC 6442, Section 3.1: either a MIME Content-ID or the SIP Content-ID MUST be used to label the location information.
sections.plainLanguage: Older rulebooks said only envelopes could have labels. This RFC adds a note to each rulebook saying the whole package can have one too.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The Content-ID value MUST NOT reveal sensitive user information. If the associated message-body is encrypted, it MUST NOT be possible to derive a decryption key from the Content-ID value.

IANA registered Content-ID in the Header Fields sub-registry of the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Parameters registry, with the reference RFC 8262 and no compact form.
sections.plainLanguage: The name tag must not give away secrets, and it must never hold a hint for opening a locked box.
